canonicalName: Transcendence of pi and the impossibility of squaring the circle

milestones.label: Constructible lengths shown to be algebraic
milestones.work: Wantzel, Recherches sur les moyens de reconnaitre si un probleme de geometrie peut se resoudre avec la regle et le compas, J. Math. Pures Appl. 2, 1837
milestones.description: Wantzel showed that lengths obtainable by ruler and compass must be algebraic, so transcendence of pi would rule out squaring the circle.

evidence.claim: Narrates Wantzel's 1837 result that constructible lengths are algebraic, so a transcendental pi would make the construction impossible.

milestones.note: No Crossref record found for the original 1837 paper (searched); year from the Wikipedia history section.

milestones.label: Hermite proves e is transcendental
milestones.work: Hermite, Sur la fonction exponentielle, Comptes Rendus 77, 1873
milestones.description: Hermite published the first proof that e is transcendental, introducing the method that Lindemann adapted nine years later.

evidence.claim: States that Hermite published the first proof of the transcendence of e in 1873 and that Lindemann used similar methods in 1882.
Crossref lists the memoir 'Sur la fonction exponentielle' in Hermite's Oeuvres (a 2009 reprint; the original 1873 Comptes Rendus run is not in Crossref).

milestones.note: Year of the original comes from the history page; Crossref only has the reprint.

milestones.label: Lindemann proves pi is transcendental
milestones.work: Lindemann, Ueber die Zahl pi, Mathematische Annalen 20, 213-225, 1882
milestones.description: Lindemann extended Hermite's method to show pi is transcendental, which together with algebraicity of constructible lengths ends the squaring problem.

evidence.claim: Record: Mathematische Annalen 20 (1882) 213-225, Lindemann, 'Ueber die Zahl pi'.
Credits Lindemann as first to prove pi transcendental, answering the classical squaring problem.
Dates the proof of impossibility to 1882 via the Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem.

milestones.note: MacTutor's squaring-the-circle topic page dates the proof to 1880; the publication record gives 1882.

milestones.label: Weierstrass gives the full theorem
milestones.work: Weierstrass, Zu Lindemann's Abhandlung 'Ueber die Ludolph'sche Zahl', Sitzungsber. Berlin, 1885
milestones.description: Weierstrass supplied a complete proof of the general statement now called the Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem, filling gaps in Lindemann's argument.

evidence.claim: Says Lindemann allowed algebraic numbers into Hermite's work in 1882 and Weierstrass shortly afterwards obtained the full result.
Crossref lists the paper in 'Pi: A Source Book' (reprint; original year not given by the record).

milestones.note: Year 1885 is the standard citation but not shown by the reprint record.

milestones.label: Hilbert's short proof
milestones.work: Hilbert, Ueber die Transcendenz der Zahlen e und pi, Math. Ann. 43, 216-219, 1893
milestones.description: Hilbert gave a much shorter proof of the transcendence of e and pi that became the textbook version.
milestones.note: Simplification, not a new result.

people.name: Charles Hermite
people.role: Proved e transcendental by an exponential-polynomial method

works.citation: Sur la fonction exponentielle, Comptes Rendus 77
Ueber die Zahl pi, Math. Ann. 20

works.whyItMatters: Full proof of the Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem

works.citation: Ueber die Transcendenz der Zahlen e und pi, Math. Ann. 43

notes: Technique transfer: Hermite's analytic transcendence method for e carried to pi and then to a ruler-and-compass impossibility via Wantzel's algebraic criterion. Wantzel's 1837 paper has no Crossref record, so its milestone rests on Wikipedia. Wantzel biography page not fetched: biographyUrl for him points to Hermite's page and should be replaced. No naming/institution milestone applies (theorem name is a later label). Weierstrass year 1885 not independently verified in a record. MacTutor topic page gives 1880 for Lindemann's proof; the journal record says 1882.

milestones.label: Grassmann's extension theory
milestones.work: Grassmann, Die lineale Ausdehnungslehre, 1844
milestones.description: Grassmann created exterior algebra and briefly noted a second product combining its elements, one root of the geometric product.

evidence.claim: States the geometric product was first briefly mentioned by Grassmann.

milestones.label: Hamilton's systematic quaternion lectures
milestones.work: Hamilton, Lectures on Quaternions, 1853
milestones.description: Hamilton's quaternion algebra, the other ingredient fused by Clifford, was set out systematically in this book.
milestones.note: Quaternions were discovered in 1843; the book is the first full public treatment.

milestones.label: Clifford's biquaternions
milestones.work: Clifford, Preliminary sketch of biquaternions, Proc. London Math. Soc. s1-4, 381-395
milestones.description: Clifford generalised quaternions to biquaternions for motions in non-Euclidean spaces, an earlier step towards his algebras.

evidence.claim: Crossref record for the paper (volume-level date 1871).

milestones.note: MacTutor says 1873; Crossref dates the volume 1871-73. Year taken from MacTutor.

milestones.label: Clifford unifies Grassmann and Hamilton
milestones.work: Clifford, Applications of Grassmann's Extensive Algebra, American Journal of Mathematics 1, 350-358, 1878
milestones.description: Clifford defined the algebra now named after him as a union of Grassmann's exterior algebra and Hamilton's quaternions.

evidence.claim: Says he introduced Clifford algebras in this 1878 paper.
Says Clifford joined Grassmann's exterior algebra to Hamilton's quaternions in 1878.

milestones.label: 'Geometric algebras' as Clifford's own term
milestones.work: Same paper (Am. J. Math. 1, 1878)
milestones.description: Clifford himself called his algebras geometric algebras, the name later revived.

evidence.claim: Notes that Clifford himself chose to call them geometric algebras.

milestones.note: Same paper as the first statement; the naming claim rests on Wikipedia only and the paper text was not read.

milestones.label: Hestenes revives geometric algebra for physics
milestones.work: Hestenes, Space-Time Algebra (1960s)
milestones.description: In the 1960s Hestenes advocated the term and framework for relativistic physics, ending a long neglect.

evidence.claim: Says the term was repopularised in the 1960s by Hestenes.
Crossref lists a 2015 Springer reissue of Space-Time Algebra.

milestones.note: Exact first edition year (1966) not confirmed in a record, so decade precision.

milestones.label: Hestenes-Sobczyk textbook
milestones.work: Hestenes and Sobczyk, Clifford Algebra to Geometric Calculus, Reidel, 1984
milestones.description: A systematic monograph presenting geometric algebra and calculus as a unified language.

notes: Hestenes' biography is not on MacTutor, so his biographyUrl points to Clifford's page; replace if needed. Lipschitz independently found related algebras around 1880 (Wikipedia, Lipschitz group) but no record was verified, so no milestone. Hestenes' first edition year not confirmed. Naming claim rests on Wikipedia.

canonicalName: Cardinality versus dimension: R^n equinumerous with R

milestones.label: Cantor's letter to Dedekind
milestones.work: Cantor to Dedekind, 1877 (private letter)
milestones.description: Cantor privately reported a one-to-one match between the interval and higher-dimensional space and was himself astonished.

evidence.claim: Says he wrote to Dedekind in 1877 proving a one-to-one correspondence between [0,1] and p-dimensional space.

milestones.note: Private letter, hence precursor.

milestones.label: Cantor's published contribution to the theory of manifolds
milestones.work: Cantor, Ein Beitrag zur Mannigfaltigkeitslehre, J. reine angew. Math. 84, 242-258, 1878
milestones.description: Cantor published the bijection between R^n and R and the notion of equivalence of sets by one-to-one correspondence.

evidence.claim: Notes the dimension paper submitted to Crelle in 1877 was delayed by Kronecker's suspicion.

milestones.note: Submitted 1877, published 1878.

milestones.label: Netto: no continuous bijection between dimensions
milestones.work: Netto, Beitrag zur Mannigfaltigkeitslehre, Crelle 86, 263-268, 1879
milestones.description: Netto showed a continuous one-to-one map cannot join spaces of different dimension, in the restricted setting of the time.

evidence.claim: Record: Crelle 86 (1879) 263-268, same title; author missing from the Crossref entry.

milestones.note: Author attribution rests on the standard citation, not on the record's metadata.

milestones.label: Peano's space-filling curve
milestones.work: Peano, Sur une courbe, qui remplit toute une aire plane, Math. Ann. 36, 157-160, 1890
milestones.description: Peano built a continuous map from the line onto a square, showing continuity alone does not protect dimension.

milestones.label: Brouwer proves invariance of dimension
milestones.work: Brouwer, Beweis der Invarianz der Dimensionenzahl, Math. Ann. 70, 161-165, 1911
milestones.description: Brouwer proved that homeomorphic Euclidean spaces have equal dimension, settling the question raised by Cantor's bijections.

evidence.claim: Associates the invariance of domain theorem with Brouwer, published 1912.

milestones.note: The domain-invariance paper is Math. Ann. 71 (1911) in Crossref, 1912 per Wikipedia.

milestones.label: Intrinsic definitions of dimension
milestones.work: Menger, Ueber die Dimensionalitaet von Punktmengen, Monatsh. Math. Phys. 33, 1923; Urysohn, Memoire sur les multiplicites Cantoriennes, Fund. Math. 7, 1925
milestones.description: Menger and Urysohn introduced topological notions of dimension defined from the space itself rather than from point counts.
milestones.note: Description based on titles and standard history; paper contents were not read.

milestones.label: Hurewicz-Wallman monograph
milestones.work: Hurewicz and Wallman, Dimension Theory, Princeton, 1941
milestones.description: First English systematic treatment of dimension theory.

evidence.claim: Archive.org record for Dimension Theory (the listed record is a later printing dated 1948).

milestones.note: First-edition year 1941 not shown by the record found; later printing 1948.

works.citation: Sur une courbe, qui remplit toute une aire plane

notes: Menger's biography page not fetched, so his biographyUrl points to Brouwer's page; replace it. Menger's 1928 Dimensionstheorie book (naming) was searched for on archive.org and not found, so no naming milestone. No first_application is established. Netto's authorship rests on the standard citation.

milestones.label: Frege's Begriffsschrift
milestones.work: Frege, Begriffsschrift, Halle, 1879
milestones.description: Frege's formal language for pure thought, the logical system on which his logicism rests.
milestones.note: A logical system, not yet the reduction of arithmetic.

milestones.label: Frege's Foundations of Arithmetic
milestones.work: Frege, Die Grundlagen der Arithmetik, Breslau, 1884
milestones.description: Frege argued that arithmetic is reducible to logic and analysed the concept of number accordingly.

evidence.claim: Cites Frege 1884, 1893, 1903 as defining mathematical notions through logical ones.

milestones.label: Frege's Grundgesetze volume I
milestones.work: Frege, Grundgesetze der Arithmetik I, Jena, 1893
milestones.description: Frege carried out the reduction in his formal system, deriving arithmetic from logical laws.

milestones.label: Russell's letter to Frege about the paradox
milestones.work: Russell to Frege, 16 June 1902 (private letter)
milestones.description: Russell pointed out that Frege's axioms yield a contradiction.

evidence.claim: States Frege received Russell's letter on 16 June 1902 pointing out the contradiction in his axioms.

milestones.note: Private; Russell found the paradox in May 1901 per MacTutor.

milestones.label: Russell's Principles of Mathematics
milestones.work: Russell, The Principles of Mathematics, 1903
milestones.description: Russell published the logicist thesis and the paradox bearing his name.

evidence.claim: Says the paradox arose while working on the Principles (1903).

milestones.label: Theory of types
milestones.work: Russell, Mathematical Logic as Based on the Theory of Types, Am. J. Math. 30, 222-262, 1908
milestones.description: Russell presented the ramified theory of types as a way to avoid the paradoxes.

evidence.claim: Says the mature theory of types appears in the 1908 article and Principia.

milestones.label: Principia Mathematica
milestones.work: Whitehead and Russell, Principia Mathematica, 3 vols, 1910-1913
milestones.description: A monumental systematic derivation of mathematics from logic using types.

works.citation: Mathematical Logic as Based on the Theory of Types

notes: Dedekind's 1888 and Peano's 1889 works were considered as precursors but the archive and Crossref searches only produced later printings or unrelated records, so no milestones. Origin of the word 'logicism' not found. No institution milestone. Frege's Grundgesetze vol. II (1903) not separately verified.

milestones.label: Fuchs on linear differential equations
milestones.work: Fuchs, Zur Theorie der linearen Differentialgleichungen mit veraenderlichen Coefficienten, Crelle 66, 121-160, 1866
milestones.description: Fuchs's study of linear equations with singular points supplied the problem that Poincare's functions were built to solve.

evidence.claim: Says Poincare named the new functions Fuchsian after Fuchs.

milestones.note: Authorship missing from the Crossref entry; the link to Poincare is through his naming.

milestones.label: Poincare's first notes on Fuchsian functions
milestones.work: Poincare, notes in Comptes Rendus, 1881
milestones.description: Poincare began publishing his theory of Fuchsian functions in 1881, linking their groups to non-Euclidean geometry.

evidence.claim: Says Poincare began publishing an outline of automorphic function theory in 1881.
Describes the insight that Fuchsian transformations are those of non-Euclidean geometry.

milestones.note: Individual notes were not located in Crossref; year from MacTutor.

milestones.label: Theory of Fuchsian groups
milestones.work: Poincare, Theorie des groupes fuchsiens, Acta Math. 1, 1-62, 1882
milestones.description: Poincare's Acta paper names and develops the groups of the theory.

evidence.claim: Says he named the functions Fuchsian after Fuchs; later called automorphic.

milestones.label: Memoir on Fuchsian functions
milestones.work: Poincare, Memoire sur les fonctions fuchsiennes, Acta Math. 1, 193-294, 1882
milestones.description: The memoir uses the new functions to solve linear differential equations.

evidence.claim: Says the functions arose from the search for solutions of differential equations.

milestones.note: That the memoir integrates linear equations is from MacTutor's account; the paper was not read.

milestones.label: Klein on Riemann function theory
milestones.work: Klein, Neue Beitraege zur Riemann'schen Functionentheorie, Math. Ann. 21, 141-218, 1883
milestones.description: Klein linked automorphic functions to Riemann surfaces and framed the uniformisation programme.

evidence.claim: Describes the Klein-Poincare race to formulate a grand uniformization theorem.

milestones.note: Paper contents not read.

milestones.label: Fricke-Klein lectures on automorphic functions
milestones.work: Fricke and Klein, Vorlesungen ueber die Theorie der automorphen Functionen, vol. 1, 1897
milestones.description: First systematic textbook treatment under the name automorphic functions.

milestones.label: Rigorous uniformisation proofs
milestones.work: Poincare, Sur l'uniformisation des fonctions analytiques, Acta Math. 31, 1-63; Koebe, Goettinger Nachrichten, 1907
milestones.description: Poincare and Koebe independently gave the first rigorous proofs of the general uniformisation theorem.

evidence.claim: Says the first rigorous proofs were by Poincare and Koebe, completed by 1907.

milestones.note: Submitted 1907, published in the 1908 volume.

works.citation: Vorlesungen ueber die Theorie der automorphen Functionen

notes: Fuchs's and Fricke's and Koebe's biography pages were not fetched; those biographyUrl values point to related MacTutor pages and should be replaced. The coinage of 'automorphic' (Klein, around 1890) is not verified, so the 1897 book is marked consolidation, not naming. The 1882 'first_application' is medium confidence.

phases: Takagi and Artin: existence and reciprocity

milestones.label: Weber on number groups in algebraic fields
milestones.work: Weber, Ueber Zahlengruppen in algebraischen Koerpern, Math. Ann. 48, 433-473, 1897
milestones.description: Weber introduced class fields as extensions attached to groups of ideal classes.

evidence.claim: Says Weber coined the term before Hilbert's papers.

milestones.note: Content not read; first Weber paper in the series (further parts: Math. Ann. 49, 50).

milestones.label: The term class field
milestones.work: Weber, Math. Ann. 48 (1897)
milestones.description: Weber coined the term class field in this period.

evidence.claim: Says it was Weber who coined the term before Hilbert's fundamental papers.

milestones.note: Exact paper for the coinage not verified; assumed from the Weber series.

milestones.label: Hilbert's Zahlbericht
milestones.work: Hilbert, Die Theorie der algebraischen Zahlkoerper, Jahresbericht DMV 4, 1897
milestones.description: A report that synthesised algebraic number theory and contains the ideas of class field theory.

evidence.claim: Says the Zahlbericht (1897) is a synthesis of Kummer, Kronecker and Dedekind and contains the ideas of class field theory.
Crossref record: modern article on the Zahlbericht.

milestones.label: Hilbert's relative abelian fields
milestones.work: Hilbert, Ueber die Theorie der relativ-Abel'schen Zahlkoerper, Goett. Nachr. 1898 (Acta Math. 26, 1902)
milestones.description: Hilbert formulated the conjectures on class fields that Takagi and Artin later proved.

evidence.claim: Says Hilbert's conjectures were proved by Takagi and Artin.

milestones.note: 1898 date is the Goettingen original; the Crossref record is the 1902 Acta version.

milestones.label: Takagi's existence theorem
milestones.work: Takagi, Ueber eine Theorie des relativ Abel'schen Zahlkoerpers, J. Coll. Sci. Tokyo 41, 1920
milestones.description: Takagi proved the classification of abelian extensions by ideal class groups.

evidence.claim: Says his most important paper of 1920 introduced Takagi class field theory.

milestones.phase: Takagi and Artin: existence and reciprocity

milestones.label: Hasse's report on class field theory
milestones.work: Hasse, Bericht ueber neuere Untersuchungen und Probleme aus der Theorie der algebraischen Zahlkoerper, 1926-1930
milestones.description: The survey that made the theory accessible.

evidence.claim: Says Hasse included Takagi's theory in his treatise on class field theory.

milestones.note: Years from standard citation; only a 1965 reprint is in Crossref.

milestones.label: Artin's general reciprocity law
milestones.work: Artin, Beweis des allgemeinen Reziprozitaetsgesetzes, Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg 5, 353-363, 1927
milestones.description: Artin proved the general reciprocity law, subsuming earlier reciprocity laws.

evidence.claim: Says he gave a general reciprocity law in 1927.

milestones.phase: Takagi and Artin: existence and reciprocity

milestones.label: Principal ideal theorem
milestones.work: Furtwaengler, Beweis des Hauptidealsatzes fuer die Klassenkoerper algebraischer Zahlkoerper, Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg 7, 14-36, 1929
milestones.description: Furtwangler used Artin's reciprocity to prove the principal ideal theorem.

evidence.claim: Calls Furtwangler's principal ideal proof the most striking application.

notes: Kronecker's 1853 abelian-extension result (Kronecker-Weber) is a precursor but no record was verified. Furtwangler's page and Kronecker's page were not fetched, Kronecker's URL points to Weber's. The 1897 naming milestone is low confidence, and the Takagi 1920 year comes from MacTutor only (Crossref lists a 1990 reprint). Chevalley's idelic work (1933, 1940) searched but not added.

milestones.label: Grassmann's extension theory
milestones.work: Grassmann, Die lineale Ausdehnungslehre, 1844
milestones.description: An algebra of vector-like quantities that later vector analysts drew on.

milestones.label: Hamilton's Lectures on Quaternions
milestones.work: Hamilton, Lectures on Quaternions, 1853
milestones.description: Quaternions, with their scalar and vector parts, were the starting point of vector analysis.

evidence.claim: Says vector calculus was developed from quaternion theory by Gibbs and Heaviside.

milestones.label: Gibbs's Elements of Vector Analysis
milestones.work: Gibbs, Elements of Vector Analysis, New Haven, 1881-1884 (privately printed)
milestones.description: Gibbs extracted vector methods from quaternions in a pamphlet for his students, apparently the first text of its kind.
milestones.note: Privately printed pamphlet in two parts (1881, 1884). The 'first text' claim is from the pamphlet's date, not a priority search.

milestones.label: Heaviside's vector treatment of electromagnetism
milestones.work: Heaviside, Electromagnetic induction and its propagation, The Electrician, 1885-1887
milestones.description: Heaviside used vector methods to restate Maxwell's theory.

evidence.claim: Says his vector methods overshadowed his electromagnetism results.

milestones.note: Dates from the Electrician series; the reprint is 2011.

milestones.label: Gibbs defends vectors against quaternionists
milestones.work: Gibbs, Quaternions and the Ausdehnungslehre, Nature 44, 79-82, 1891
milestones.description: A public exchange in Nature made the case for vector analysis over quaternions.

milestones.label: Gibbs-Wilson Vector Analysis
milestones.work: Gibbs and Wilson, Vector Analysis, Yale, 1901
milestones.description: The textbook that fixed the notation and terminology.

evidence.claim: Says most notation was established by the 1901 book.

notes: Wilson's page not fetched, URL points to Gibbs. Heaviside's Electromagnetic Theory vol. 1 (1893, archive.org record exists) is not used as a milestone as its vector chapter was not read. Origin of the name 'vector analysis' not established.

canonicalName: Weil's dictionary: number fields, function fields, Riemann surfaces

milestones.label: Dedekind-Weber algebraic functions
milestones.work: Dedekind and Weber, Theorie der algebraischen Functionen einer Veraenderlichen, Crelle 92, 181-290, 1882
milestones.description: They treated algebraic functions by the same ideal-theoretic means as number fields.
milestones.note: Content not read; claim based on the standard account.

milestones.label: Artin on quadratic function fields
milestones.work: Artin, Quadratische Koerper im Gebiete der hoeheren Kongruenzen, Math. Z. 19, 153-206, 1924
milestones.description: Artin formulated the zeta function of function fields over finite fields with its Riemann hypothesis.
milestones.note: Content not read.

milestones.label: Hasse: Riemann hypothesis for elliptic function fields
milestones.work: Hasse, Zur Theorie der abstrakten elliptischen Funktionenkoerper I-III, Crelle 175, 1936
milestones.description: Hasse proved the Riemann hypothesis for elliptic curves over finite fields.
milestones.note: Proof content stated from standard history.

milestones.label: Weil on the number field/function field analogy
milestones.work: Weil, Sur l'analogie entre les corps de nombres algebriques et les corps de fonctions algebriques, 1939
milestones.description: Weil stated the analogy explicitly.
milestones.note: Year 1939 is from the original journal, not from the reprint record.

milestones.label: Weil on algebraic functions with finite constant field
milestones.work: Weil, Sur les fonctions algebriques a corps de constantes fini, C. R. Acad. Sci. 210, 1940
milestones.description: Weil announced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis for curves using geometry on the curve.

evidence.claim: Says he proved the Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields while in prison.

milestones.note: Year 1940 from the original, not from the reprint.

milestones.label: Weil conjectures
milestones.work: Weil, Numbers of solutions of equations in finite fields, Bull. AMS 55, 497-508, 1949
milestones.description: Weil stated conjectures for zeta functions of varieties.

evidence.claim: Says in 1949 he raised these conjectures.

milestones.label: Deligne proves the last Weil conjecture
milestones.work: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil I, Publ. IHES 43, 273-307, 1974
milestones.description: Deligne proved the analogue of the Riemann hypothesis.

evidence.claim: Says the analogue of the Riemann hypothesis was proved by Deligne.

works.citation: Numbers of solutions of equations in finite fields

notes: Weil's 1940 letter from prison to his sister Simone, containing the 'Rosetta stone' account, is private and was not verified. Only reprint records exist for Weil's early papers, so 1939 and 1940 rest on original-journal years from the original journal citation, not verified in a record (low/medium). No consolidation or institution milestone found.

milestones.label: Hamilton's icosian calculus
milestones.work: Hamilton, icosian calculus, 1856
milestones.description: Hamilton described the icosahedral group via the dodecahedron's edge graph.

evidence.claim: Notes a proto-form in Hamilton's 1856 icosian calculus.

milestones.note: Year from Wikipedia only.

milestones.label: von Dyck's group-theoretic studies
milestones.work: von Dyck, Gruppentheoretische Studien, Math. Ann. 20, 1-44, 1882
milestones.description: First systematic study of groups by generators and relations.

evidence.claim: Says Dyck laid the foundations in the early 1880s.

milestones.label: Poincare's fundamental group
milestones.work: Poincare, Analysis situs, 1895
milestones.description: Poincare introduced the fundamental group, giving presentations a topological role.

evidence.claim: Says he introduced the fundamental group in his 1894 paper and the Analysis situs was published 1895.

milestones.note: MacTutor mentions both 1894 and 1895.

milestones.label: Tietze presents the fundamental group
milestones.work: Tietze, Ueber die topologischen Invarianten mehrdimensionaler Mannigfaltigkeiten, Monatsh. Math. Phys. 19, 1-118, 1908
milestones.description: Tietze produced finite presentations of fundamental groups and the transformations showing they are invariants.

evidence.claim: Describes the finite presentation and Tietze transformations.

milestones.label: Dehn's infinite discontinuous groups
milestones.work: Dehn, Ueber unendliche diskontinuierliche Gruppen, Math. Ann. 71, 116-144, 1911
milestones.description: Dehn posed the word and isomorphism problems.

evidence.claim: Says he formulated the word and isomorphism problems.

milestones.label: Nielsen and Schreier on free groups
milestones.work: Nielsen, Math. Ann. 91, 1924; Schreier, Abh. Hamburg 5, 1927
milestones.description: Nielsen's method and Schreier's subgroup theorem for free groups.

milestones.label: Undecidability of the word problem
milestones.work: Boone, The word problem, Annals of Math. 70, 207, 1959
milestones.description: Boone proved a finitely presented group with unsolvable word problem exists.
milestones.note: Novikov proved the same independently around 1955; Novikov's record not checked.

milestones.label: Magnus-Karrass-Solitar
milestones.work: Magnus, Karrass, Solitar, Combinatorial Group Theory, 1966
milestones.description: First systematic text.

notes: Dyck's page not available on MacTutor. Dyck, Schreier URLs point to related pages. The name 'combinatorial group theory' pre-1966 use was searched in Crossref and not found. Novikov 1955 not verified.

aliases: Galois theory of linear differential equations

milestones.label: Picard on algebraic groups of transformations
milestones.work: Picard, Sur les equations differentielles lineaires et les groupes algebriques de transformations, Ann. Toulouse 1, A1-A15, 1887
milestones.description: Picard associated algebraic transformation groups to linear differential equations.

milestones.label: Vessiot's thesis
milestones.work: Vessiot, Sur l'integration des equations differentielles lineaires, Ann. ENS 9, 197-280, 1892
milestones.description: Vessiot developed the Picard-Vessiot theory using Lie groups.

evidence.claim: Says the thesis is what is now called the Picard-Vessiot theory.

milestones.label: Vessiot on Galois generalisations
milestones.work: Vessiot, Sur la theorie de Galois et ses diverses generalisations, Ann. ENS 21, 9-85, 1904
milestones.description: Vessiot extended Galois theory beyond linear equations.
milestones.note: Content not read.

milestones.label: Kolchin's algebraic matric groups
milestones.work: Kolchin, Annals of Math. 49, 1948
milestones.description: Kolchin recast the theory using algebraic groups.

evidence.claim: Says he became a pioneer of linear algebraic groups while applying Ritt's theory to Picard-Vessiot.

milestones.label: Galois theory of differential fields
milestones.work: Kolchin, Am. J. Math. 75, 753, 1953
milestones.description: Extension to strongly normal extensions.
milestones.note: Content not read.

milestones.label: Kolchin's book
milestones.work: Kolchin, Differential Algebra and Algebraic Groups, Academic Press, 1973
milestones.description: Systematic monograph.

evidence.claim: Lists the book in its sources.
Mentions 1973 in connection with the book.

milestones.note: Year from Wikipedia sources; no archive record found.

works.citation: Sur les equations differentielles lineaires et les groupes algebriques de transformations
Sur l'integration des equations differentielles lineaires
Algebraic matric groups and the Picard-Vessiot theory
Differential Equations from the Algebraic Standpoint
